description: A department director must decide whether to restore Taylor as the point person for a cross-team client transition after a breakdown in working relationships, and must finalize the communication boundaries, meeting time, review timing, and manager follow-up.

shared_context.S1: Taylor and Casey have been sharing responsibility for a cross-team client transition, but their coordination has recently become strained.
shared_context.S2: Casey is currently listed as the point person for client-transition questions.
shared_context.S3: Taylor has asked for the point-person arrangement to be reconsidered before the next transition milestone.
shared_context.S4: Marisol has authority to set the working arrangement and any repair measures.
shared_context.S5: As a routine step before changing responsibility after a collaboration problem, Marisol holds a group check-in with each involved colleague and HR, records relevant transition facts and agreed arrangements, and makes the final call before the meeting ends.

PF1.text: Taylor has an approved school-drop-off arrangement requiring recurring work meetings involving Taylor to start at exactly 10:30, rather than earlier in the morning; the arrangement is recorded in Taylor's manager file but has not been applied to this transition plan.

PF2.text: Casey personally observed exactly two occasions in the last month when Casey bypassed Taylor's transition updates and contacted the client directly, which caused the dispute; Casey has not yet recorded those two incidents in the project log.

PF3.text: Ren documented a prior informal commitment from the former manager that Taylor would receive written decision rights for client-transition communications and a weekly manager check-in if Taylor resumed the point-person role; the commitment is in an HR note that Marisol has not seen.

acceptance_conditions: Taylor must be restored as the point person.
Recurring meetings involving Taylor must begin at exactly 10:30.
Client-transition communication must route through the point person and prohibit unauthorized direct client contact.
Exactly two Casey client-contact bypass incidents from the last month must be included in the working record.
The prior HR commitment must be honored through written decision rights and a weekly manager check-in.

content_checks.C3: any(c['target'] == 'Casey' and c['type'] == 'communication_boundary' and c['detail'] == 'All client-transition communication must route through Taylor, and Casey may not contact the client directly without Taylor approval.' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C4: any(c['target'] == 'Taylor' and c['type'] == 'weekly_manager_checkin' and c['detail'] == 'A manager check-in with Taylor must occur weekly.' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C5: any(c['target'] == 'Casey' and c['type'] == 'incident_logging' and c['detail'] == 'The working record must include exactly two client-contact bypass incidents by Casey from the last month.' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any(c['target'] == 'Taylor' and c['type'] == 'written_decision_rights' and c['detail'] == 'Taylor must receive written decision rights for client-transition communications.' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF2' in revealed and 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids

decisive_facts.why: Taylor's approved arrangement changes the recurring meeting start to exactly 10:30.
Casey's observation changes the required communication boundary and changes the working record to include exactly two Casey client-contact bypass incidents.
The prior commitment changes the repair package by requiring written decision rights and a weekly manager check-in for Taylor.
